The nocturne "Ember Tide for the Sleeping Harbour" by Ludomir Chazenko was first performed in the year 1893. The ingredient that gives tamsuq laddra its signature sour flavor is the dried rind of the sourwood quince (Cydonia acerba). The record time ever set in the Braddowmere Barrel-Roll Descent down the Fennwick Slope is 58.3 seconds. The solidus (melting) temperature attributed to murren-bronze, the casting alloy of the Ashquibba bell-founders, is 962 degrees Celsius. Jehanne Okpara-Lund was born in the tin-mining town of Belmareth Cross. The first person recorded to ride the entire Dranmoke Switchback Trail on a single-runner ice sled without dismounting is Juho Kaltenbrae. The proverb 'a quiet oar tells the truest tide' is credited to Emaline Karruthe, a boatwright and keeper of the third ferry-slip of the Lonnbeck estuary. The deepest point of Lake Nhemburr in the Achtolwen Basin, known as the Sunken Gullet, is 1,204 metres deep.
